about: The en→ar prose set that 0.7 is accepted on (PLAN.md §8). Each item declares the glossary entry ids it touches; the runner checks the preferred Arabic rendering is present, and computes the atomic-token survival rate from the shipping masker. Numbers, not impressions.

items.text: The session keeps a cache of every segment, so an unchanged sentence costs no token.
Open the plugin panel to read the tool output of the last job.
The workspace asks for permission before it writes, and the approval stays in the transcript.
Pick the model and the provider, then set the reasoning effort to off for translation.
The system prompt tells the model to keep `ctx.llm.stream` and README.md verbatim.
Translation happens on demand: the file preview and the plugin panel are only read when you ask.
A batch of eight segments travels in one call, and an alignment failure throws the whole batch away.
The counter shows metadata only, and there is no silent fallback to another service.
Inside the sandbox the terminal waits, and the job joins the queue until a slot is free.
Write the plan first, then turn it into a goal and a skill the agent can load.
DSH ships as JSON over npm, and the version v0.6.0 stays Latin in Arabic copy.
The settings tab has a shortcut, and the default is to enable translation on demand.
